# Requirements-to-needs adequacy

To infer that a need is met from fulfilled requirements, explain why those requirements are enough to meet the need in the stated circumstances, and establish that the system or combined arrangement satisfies the required combination of them. Meeting an incomplete set of requirements does not establish need fulfillment. Evidence about the actual outcome can support or contradict the conclusion.

When a meaning needed for that judgment is unclear, raise the ambiguity. The environment determines how or whether it is handled. Any conclusion depending on missing clarification remains unknown; an independently established failure can still justify an unmet result. Manifold does not require a particular human, orchestrator, handler or response procedure.

Adopt the [successful, unsuccessful and ambiguous report-review cases](../../standard/ontology/concepts/requirement.md#from-requirement-fulfillment-to-need-fulfillment) as illustrations of this rule. These hypothetical cases distinguish need fulfillment, requirements fulfilled despite an unmet need, and unresolved meaning. They are not evidence of real-world operation.
